craft_rationale.audience_need: The audience already watched Willa read the false weight alone last night. They now need that private craft-fact to hit the only relationship that can make the theme expensive: she has to put the piece in front of the man who raised her, and he has to say the weld and the levy in the same room, in work-language, without a verdict. They need to hear that the compact is currently a seventy-one-year-old body, and they need the old reasons (the slide, a village that would have come apart without a weight) left audible so the scene is a debt problem, not a villain unmasking.
craft_rationale.genre_convention: Low-fantasy screenplay, plain register, seventy percent dialogue. Revelation is two people and a piece of metal at a bench, not a lore monologue or a magical vision. Binding is spoken as cost and work. No swelling pardon, no speech that solves the moral math. The forge-house stays the unit of space; the village does not enter.
craft_rationale.dramatic_function: Discharges pl-02:st5, admission_of_the_weld. Converts relic_knowledge from a secret Willa can still put back into a spoken account that cannot be unspoken. Opens the next practical questions she is built to ask — who pays when he cannot, what the house owes the village, whether a working lie that was paid for in marrow is still a lie — and prevents trust_in_orren from sitting at a comfortable seventy. Irreversible inside the house.
craft_rationale.why_now: ev-007 left the reading inside the house overnight. That is the longest she can hold a named fault without taking it to the maker; another day would be complicity, and she thinks in work-order. His body is already failing, so delay risks the levy ending unspoken and leaving her a dead man's bomb. Earlier, before she could read the weld herself, would have been his confession unearned: she has to arrive as a smith who saw the join, not as a daughter he decided to unburden. Later, after a public step, would skip the intimate account and damn him before the levy is even named.
alternatives_rejected: Orren confesses unprompted before she sets the piece down — steals her agency and starts redeeming him as the man who came clean.
She takes the weight to the elders first — skips the house, turns him into a public fraud before the levy is understood, and betrays her habit of treating faults as maker-business.
He denies the weld and she has to pry — flattens forty years of paying into simple lying and loses the old reasons.
Tearful hug, 'I did it to keep you fed,' or any bid for instant pardon — cheap redemption, forbidden by the root.
He asks her in this scene to take the levy onto her own body — dumps the next plot hinge into this beat and makes him selfish in the simple way the root forbids.
A long explanation of how binding-magic works — violates plain register and her way of thinking in work.
She already understands the levy before he speaks — undercuts the admission the node is required to discharge.

perception.sight: Thin morning through the forge-house shutters; dust in the shaft. Orren already up, smaller in the chair by the banked hearth than he is at the anvil. She watches his hands first, as she always does — knuckle swell, the old burn on the left thumb — then the place on the bench where she will put the piece. In better light than last night the hairline weld is an insult, too clean, forty years of someone keeping a join from speaking. His eyes go to her grip before they go to her face.
perception.sound: Banked forge, no working ring. His breath measured the way she has learned to measure it. Her own boots on packed earth, too loud. The particular note of the false weight when she sets it on wood — slightly dead, the note she heard last night and could not unhear. Village waking somewhere beyond the door, a hinge, a dog, none of it invited in. When he finally answers, the voice is lower than instruction-voice.
perception.touch: Frost still in both hands from the overnight reading; the metal drinks heat out of her palms and does not give it back. Grain of the bench under her wrist. She does not want to let the piece go and does not want to keep holding it. If her knuckle brushes his when she slides it across, his skin is paper-dry and too cold for the hearth.
perception.smell: Banked coal, his joint liniment, last night's scale, the faint sour of an old body that slept in the chair. The piece itself almost odorless — a good forgery. Her own unslept sweat in the wool at her collar.
perception.taste: Sleep-sour, unwashed mouth. She has not eaten. A copper edge as if she bit the cheek in the night and is only now tasting it.
perception.interoception: Cold that will not leave the fingers, a tightness under the sternum that she files as unpaid account rather than fear. Hunger second. The particular fatigue of carrying a true reading across a night without putting it down. Breath a little high. The frost feels like the piece is still claiming a small levy from her just for having been read.

appraisal.value_at_stake: The work-truth of the village weight; the house that took her in; what she owes the man who taught her to see a weld versus what a false weight owes every stall in the market; whether her competence at reading metal has just made her the person who has to break the house.
appraisal.self_conscious_emotion: Apprentice-shame at having to name a master's fault, mixed with the uneasy obligation of a girl who does not know which ledger — house or village — gets the next line.
appraisal.moral_reading: The weld is a fact and a fault. Forty years of a body paying is also a fact, not yet a pardon. She is not ready to call it theft or sacrifice; she is ready to ask what is still owed and who is paying.

norms_in_force: A fault in the metal goes to the maker before it goes to the street.
Apprentice does not accuse master in front of the village.
House business stays in the house until the house has spoken.
The village weight is public trust; a smith's word on it is supposed to be clean.
You do not throw away the person who pulled you out of a dead camp when you were a child, not in one morning.
social_norms.how_others_would_judge: Elders would say she should have walked the piece to the hall at first light. Other smiths would say she did the right first thing — take a join to the one who laid it. The village, if they ever hear she sat on a false weight overnight, will split between 'loyal girl' and 'she protected the cheat.'
social_norms.standing_at_risk: Her place in the forge-house, the unspoken inheritance of the anvil, Orren's trust, and any future standing as the person who either kept the compact or broke it by speaking.

theory_of_mind.d1: She believes Orren already knows she has read it — he taught her the eye that found the join — and that he has been paying something hidden for years that matches the failing body. She believes he is afraid of her face more than of the elders.
theory_of_mind.d2: She believes he believes she is still loyal enough to bring the piece inside the house rather than down the hill, and that she still trusts him enough to let him speak. She thinks he is counting on the raising.
theory_of_mind.d3: She believes he believes she already thinks the house comes first, and that she will treat the weld as work to be accounted rather than as a crime to be cried in the square — that he thinks she still believes he is the man who does not waste metal or children.

urges.cravings: For him to take the piece out of the space between them and make the account balance in one work-sentence. Heat in the hands. Not to have to be the adult in the room.
urges.physical_needs: Warmth in frosted fingers, food, the sleep she did not take, a bench to lean her weight on so the shaking does not show.
urges.psych_needs_conscious: A craft explanation: why this weld, what levy, what happens to the compact when the body in the chair can no longer pay. She needs him to talk in joins and costs, not in love.
urges.psych_needs_unconscious: Permission to remain the apprentice. For the only parent she has not to become a forger in a single answer. For someone older to settle the debt-account so she is not the one who decides what is owed.

impairments.physical: Hands frosted: reduced grip, pain on close work, fine motor shake she will hide by setting the piece down early.
impairments.medical: None named beyond exhaustion and the cold injury in the hands.
impairments.magical: Residual claim from reading a bound forgery overnight; the frost is the piece answering her, a small unauthorized levy for having seen the join.
impairments.coercive: The compact itself — she cannot smash, hide, or parade the weight without spending other people's trade. The unpaid debt of being raised in this house, which sits on her mouth when she wants to use harder words.

options_weighed: Walk the piece to the elders at first light and let the hall name it forgery.
Put it back in the chest, unsay the reading, keep house peace.
Bring the reading to Orren now, inside, and make him speak the weld.
Sit on it until his body finishes dying and inherit the problem as a corpse's secret.
deliberation.reasoning: Public first would break the house and maybe the compact before she understands what is paying to keep the weight 'true.' Silence would be a lie in the work, and she cannot hold a lie she has already weighed. Waiting for his death is cowardice and leaves the levy with no living name. Taking it to the maker is both smith-protocol and the only way her unsettled account knows how to move.
deliberation.chosen_because: She still trusts him enough (seventy) to give the question to him first, and she thinks in work: a fault goes to the one who laid the join. The practical question — what does this cost, and who is still paying — cannot be asked of the square.

control.felt: Cold grief, a clean anger she will not name because naming it would turn him into a criminal before the levy is spoken, and the child-fear of losing the house with one sentence.
control.expressed: Practical craft questions. She sets the weight down, names the false mass, names the forty-year weld, and stops. She does not raise her voice. She does not say father, and she does not say thief.
control.divergence_reason: If the grief or anger comes out first she becomes the accuser and he becomes the dock, and she does not yet know if that reading is true. Apprentice habit: you do not shout in the forge-house, and you do not spend words the work has not earned.

Willa.intention: Make him name what she already read so the account is spoken inside the house and she can see what, practically, is owed next.
Willa.action: She brings the recovered piece to him in the morning, sets it on the bench between his hands and hers, and says the weld is his and the weight is false. Then she waits through his silence and does not soften the wait.

trajectory.shift: Overnight clench becomes a decision to treat the reading as maker-business rather than as a secret or a public cry. Frost still in the hands; debt-account still unsettled.
trajectory.trigger: Dawn, him awake in the chair, the piece still in the house from ev-007.

trajectory.shift: Private knowledge becomes a shared object on the bench. She moves from holder-of-the-reading to smith-naming-a-fault. Trust is no longer a stored number; it is being spent in front of her.
trajectory.trigger: The dead note of the weight on wood; his eyes going to her frosted grip.

trajectory.shift: The levy named — not just a false join but forty years of his body paying to keep the compact standing. Moral confusion spikes instead of resolving: the forgery is also a sacrifice. Trust complicates rather than cleanly drops.
trajectory.trigger: He says he bound the levy to himself after the slide.

trajectory.shift: She does not absolve and does not condemn. She asks the next work-question: what happens when he cannot pay. She leaves the unit knowing the village weight is a dying man's hidden cost, and the account is more unsettled, not less.
trajectory.trigger: The silence after the admission, which she refuses to fill with comfort or with a sentence that would let either of them off.

decision: Willa brings the false weight to Orren inside the forge-house at first light and names the forty-year weld in craft terms; he admits he made the piece after the original was lost in the slide and bound the hidden levy to his own failing body so the compact would hold. She does not take it to the village. He does not ask pardon. Neither tries to settle what is owed in this scene; the admission is the whole spend.
